title: Staged GTM sprint template for model variants and localization
creator: Lena Park
description: Reusable staged go-to-market (GTM) sprint template to coordinate catalog addition of new model variants (quantized / full-precision / distilled) with localization, benchmark publication, docs, and announcement assets. The goal is to reduce coordination overhead, clarify owner handoffs, and ensure release notes and operational dashboards are ready at publish time.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog entry published with correct metadata (model id, variant tags, compute profiles, recommended quantization).
Benchmarks published in the public catalog page and internal dashboard with latency/cost/quality baselines for common prompt sets.
Documentation updated: quickstart, migration notes, config examples, and localization strings for en-US + first two target languages.
Release notes drafted, reviewed by Legal/Security, and scheduled in the release channel with links to PRs and dashboards.
Support playbook and observability dashboards (per-route cost & token breakdown) created and linked in the console.
checklist: Week 0: Intake -- confirm model variant names, compatibility matrix, and required hardware targets; owner + backup assigned.
Week 1: Engineering -- model onboarding (container + weights), perf smoke tests on canary infra, and create ENG PR for runtime config (kernel hints, kv cache flags).
Week 1: Benchmarks -- define benchmark prompt set (representative prompts), run batch and p95 latency experiments, collect throughput/cost numbers, and snapshot outputs for quality checks.
Week 2: Docs -- write quickstart, migration notes for customers using older model versions, sample SDK snippets for streaming and function-calling; start localization passes for primary locales.
Week 2: Console & Observability -- add model to catalog UI, set default routing policies, create per-model dashboard card, and wire telemetry tags for billing and latency SLOs.
Week 3: Release notes & Comm -- draft release notes with breaking changes, recommended configs, and known limitations; coordinate internal announcement and public blog draft cadence.
Week 3: Legal & Compliance -- validate model license and include required attribution, confirm no restricted data in training artifacts; escalate if third-party license issues found.
Week 4: Readiness review -- cross-functional checklist walk-through (PM, ENG, DESIGN, SRE, LEGAL, SUPPORT), sign-off matrix completed, and fallback plan documented.
Production release: Monitor first 48 hours for error spikes, token cost anomalies, and customer support queues; prepare fast rollback plan mapping to previous model variant.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Quantized variant shows lower quality on hallucination-sensitive prompts. Mitigation: Add a ‘recommended_for’ tag in catalog and include explicit migration note; run targeted evals and add guardrail examples in readme.

Risk: Localization delays push the public announcement date. Mitigation: Publish English release notes + product page and schedule localized updates as follow-up patches with clear versioning and banners in the console.

Risk: Unexpected runtime kernel regression. Mitigation: Canary rollout to 5% traffic, compare p95 latency and error rates vs baseline; auto-fallback to previous kernel or model variant if thresholds are exceeded.

Risk: License attribution missing for a third-party component. Mitigation: Hold public release until Legal signs off; prepare a statement and service notice if late attribution discovered post-release.
release_notes_outline: Headline: New model family ‘Aurora’ with triple variants for latency/cost/accuracy trade-offs.
Summary: Short blurb describing ideal use-cases for each variant and recommended default configs.
Migration notes: Config snippets for SDK and REST calls, breaking changes (if parameter name changed), and rollback instructions.
Benchmarks: Table snapshots for p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and per-1M-token cost for each variant on typical sequence lengths.
Known limitations & guidance: Hallucination cases, prompt patterns to avoid, recommended timeout and token limits.
Links: Catalog page, benchmark dashboard, GitHub PRs, support playbook, and blog draft.
supporting_assets: Design: catalog card mocks (DES-210 review feedback in comments)
Engineering: runtime config PR (ENG-8842) and canary deployment playbook
Benchmarks: canonical prompt set + raw output archive
Docs: localization spreadsheet and content freeze checklist
